A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Mixture of Decoders work and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–E. Matching relocated material and inspecting the visual content supports a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original layer-reconstruction, sparse-probing, feature-steering, and ablation results across several language models.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds Gemma2-27B reconstruction results, computational benchmarks, and shared-expert weight analysis.

M1.justification: The Hadamard-factorized decoder weights, sparse routing, forward pass, reconstruction objective, and GLU extension remain unchanged. Random-K training already appeared in v1 Appendix C.2; v2 Appendix A.6 explains the existing TopK operation without changing the method.

E1.justification: OpenWebText reconstruction and generation, the 24 sample-level probing tasks, and the 10 token-level probing tasks are retained. Gemma2-27B adds a model configuration within the existing reconstruction task, without introducing a new dataset, domain, or task requirement.

E2.justification: Transcoders, Skip Transcoders, TopK-SAEs, and µMoEs retain their roles in the corresponding comparisons. The Gemma2-27B experiment uses the existing Transcoder/Skip Transcoder comparators, while the computational benchmark compares against the existing sparse-MLP model form.

E3.justification: v2 adds a partially trained Gemma2-27B configuration and a controlled computational benchmark with batch size 512 and specified layer dimensions. The reported output-faithfulness continuation length also changes from 32 tokens in v1 Appendix B.1 to 16 in v2 Section 3.1.2. The corresponding plots are unchanged, so this does not establish that those experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 Appendix B.6 adds computational-cost analysis and benchmarking. Appendix C.2/Table 9 adds a diagnostic testing whether the shared expert simply reproduces the original decoder, using weight-matrix distances. Existing rank, encoder, sparsity, feature-balance, and random-K analyses are retained.

E5.justification: The new NeurIPS checklist, item 7, explicitly acknowledges the absence of statistical-significance reporting and says repeat training was infeasible under the resource budget. This adds information about repeat-run feasibility, without establishing additional runs. The existing seed-42 disclosure and normalized-rank variability reporting are unchanged.

E6.justification: New v2 Table 3 reports Gemma2-27B normalized MSE after 50k iterations: 0.069 for MxD, 0.119 for Transcoder, and 0.093 for Skip Transcoder. Table 6 adds computational measurements, including latency of 1.457 ms for MxD versus 1.394 ms for Sparse MLP. Table 9 adds decoder-distance results. These are bounded additions; the existing plotted results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: v2 Appendix B.6/Table 5 adds theoretical parameter and FLOP expressions, including the parameter-matching relation H = N + H* and an additional O/2 FLOPs for MxD under its counting convention. The rank-preservation lemmas, forward-pass proof, and GLU/MoV derivations remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution list, and conclusion retain the central claims of faithful layer-level sparse decomposition, rank preservation, superior sparsity–accuracy performance, and competitive feature specialization. The additional experiments support these claims without redefining the principal contribution.

C2.justification: v2 replaces the specific low-learning-rate caution with discussion of random initialization, expert diversity, and possible future balancing or diversity mechanisms. It interprets the new weight-distance diagnostic as evidence against copying the original decoder. It also adds a substantive warning about LLM-judge reliability and cautions against overinterpreting absolute steering scores.

D1.justification: v2 documents the Gemma2-27B half-precision setup, reduced batch/buffer sizes, feature multiplier, target layer, and training budget. It specifies computational-benchmark dimensions and FLOP-counting conventions, clarifies which parameters are trained, and explains TopK including its tie-handling limitation. Existing code links, resource tables, and steering prompts are retained.

R1.justification: Section 4 adds an interpretability-by-design paragraph positioning MxDs relative to bilinear, combinatorial, and tensor-network approaches. Additional citations cover cross-layer linear transformations, expert balancing/diversity, LLM judges, and FLOP counting; the SAE training-tricks citation is removed. The main positioning against sparse MLPs and parameter-efficient MoEs remains stable.

P1.justification: Output-faithfulness material moves from Appendix B.1 into a new main-text Section 3.1.2. v2 adds a NeurIPS checklist, localized explanatory subsections, expanded acknowledgments, and author/contact/publication-header edits. Most scientific prose and the overall section organization are retained.

P2.justification: v2 corrects dimension labels in Figure 1, merges v1 Figures 6–7 into main-text Figure 4, and adds four tables covering Gemma2-27B, theoretical costs, measured costs, and decoder distances. Existing plots and qualitative examples are retained with relocation and renumbering, without a broad visual redesign.

improvement.justification: v2 supplies useful evidence missing from v1 about computational cost, larger-model reconstruction, and shared-expert behavior, while adding clearer qualifications about collapse and LLM-based evaluation. These strengthen scrutiny and documentation of the existing claims. The gains remain limited: the Gemma2-27B comparison is partially trained at one layer, the weight diagnostic is narrow, and repeated-run validation remains absent.
